pull.title: feat(harnesses): one registry per coding agent, and real model metadata in every catalogue it generates
pull.body:
## What was wrong

Every catalogue MCC generated for a coding agent contained the same invented numbers for every model.

`cli/launchers/codex_model_catalog.py:151-183` built **the same dict for every model**, varying only `slug`, `display_name` and `priority`:

```python
"context_window": 200000,
"max_context_window": 200000,
"effective_context_window_percent": 95,
"experimental_supported_tools": [],
"input_modalities": ["text"],
```

and applied the same fixed four reasoning rungs to everything (`SUPPORTED_REASONING_LEVELS`, `:16-27`). Pi's bundled extension had the same shape of problem one level down — `pi_extension.ts:6-7` hard-coded `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 128000` and `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 16384`, and `:65` emitted `cost: {input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0}` for every model.

Neither could have done better. Both were built from `GET /v1/models`, whose `ModelResponse` (`api/model_catalog.py:32-39`) carries an id, a display name, a timestamp and **no capability fields at all**. The launchers run in their own processes with no `RequestRuntimePort`, so the resolution ladder — which already resolves per-model context length, output ceiling, vision, tool support and effort vocabulary, and renders all of it on the Models page — was unreachable from the code that had to publish it.

Measured on a scratch server with four models whose real limits differ by two orders of magnitude:

```
BEFORE custom_acme/openai/gpt-5-nano                    context_window= 200000 rungs= ['low','medium','high','xhigh'] modalities= ['text']
BEFORE custom_acme/google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview  context_window= 200000 rungs= ['low','medium','high','xhigh'] modalities= ['text']
BEFORE custom_acme/anthropic/claude-opus-4-7            context_window= 200000 rungs= ['low','medium','high','xhigh'] modalities= ['text']
```

An 8k model and a 1M model were advertised to Codex's picker as identical.

Separately, three ids — `claude`, `codex`, `pi` — were written out by hand in `pyproject.toml`, both installers (three lists each), `mcc-help`, `RtkState`, `_ALL_AGENTS`, the tray menu and the dashboard. Eight places to forget one.

## What this changes

**One registry.** `config/harnesses.py` declares each coding-agent CLI once: id, display name, binary, protocol, install hint (with a Windows override), console-script commands, catalogue format and filename, passthrough subcommands, binary-identity markers, and RTK capability with its enable/uninstall arguments. `mcc-help`, the RTK state file's keys, the RTK CLI, the tray menu, the dashboard and both installers' three lists are generated from or checked against it. It holds data only and lives under `config/` because `api/` may not import `cli/` (`tests/contracts/test_import_boundaries.py`); `cli/harnesses/registry.py` binds a spec to launcher behaviour and is the one place the never-install rule is enforced.

**One neutral record.** `application/catalogue_model.py` builds a `CatalogueModel` per routable model from the ladder — context length, output ceiling, vision, tool support (derived from the gateway's published `supported_parameters`, never assumed), the full `ModelReasoningCapability`, prices, and per-field provenance. Every capability field is `X | None`, and `None` means *no source stated this*. It reuses `build_models_list_response`'s visibility filter, ref enumeration and two-variant projection, so a model cannot appear in one and not the other.

**Thin per-CLI serialisers.** `application/catalogues/{codex,pi}.py`, one pure function each. Effort vocabularies are *intersected* with the CLI's own rungs, never extended. Where a CLI's schema makes a field optional, an unknown omits the key; where it requires a value, the serialiser uses **that CLI's** documented default from a module-level `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS` and records the substitution — visible in the file's `_mcc_defaulted` block, on the launcher's stderr, and on the dashboard card.

**A capability-bearing route.** `GET /admin/api/catalogue-models` (loopback-only) returns the neutral records plus each harness's already-serialised document. `mcc-codex` and the Pi extension fetch that instead of `/v1/models` and write the bytes they are handed, so the launch-time path and the background refresh cannot drift. `/v1/models` is untouched — it is an Anthropic-compatible payload Claude Code itself consumes.

**A fan-out publisher.** `runtime/harness_catalogues.py` replaces `CodexModelCatalogPublisher` on the identical `cache_model_infos` → `_publish_model_catalog` trigger. Because it builds from the ladder, **a capability change with no change to the model list now re-emits every catalogue**, which was not true before. It refreshes only files that already exist; the one exception is `~/.fcc/codex-model-catalog.json`, created at startup because the Codex App reads it from a persistent `config.toml` and has no launcher.

## What to expect

Codex's `/model` picker now shows each model's real window and only the reasoning rungs that model actually publishes. Same server, same four models, after:

```
AFTER  custom_acme/openai/gpt-5-nano                    context_window= 400000  rungs= ['low','medium','high']            modalities= ['text','image']
AFTER  custom_acme/google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview  context_window= 8192    rungs= ['low','medium','high','xhigh']    modalities= ['text']
AFTER  custom_acme/anthropic/claude-opus-4-7            context_window= 1000000 rungs= ['low','medium','high','xhigh']    modalities= ['text','image']
AFTER  custom_acme/openai/gpt-4o                        context_window= 128000  rungs= []                                modalities= ['text','image']
AFTER top-level keys: ['_mcc_defaulted', 'models']
```

`gpt-5-nano` loses `xhigh` because it never claimed it. `gpt-4o` gets no effort list at all because the ladder knows it does not reason. Nothing invented survives: the launcher says so on stderr —

```
My Claude Code: 6 model(s) use Codex's own defaults where no provider published a value:
  custom_acme/acme/no-such-model-xyz: context_window, max_context_window, input_modalities, supported_reasoning_levels, default_reasoning_level, supports_reasoning_summaries, supports_parallel_tool_calls
  custom_acme/anthropic/claude-opus-4-7: supports_parallel_tool_calls
  ...
```

A new **Coding agents** dashboard page lists every registered harness with its installed state, command, protocol, catalogue path, last-written timestamp, model count, defaulted-model count and RTK toggle. The RTK checkboxes on the Providers page are now generated from the same list.

**Models whose real window is under 200000 will stop claiming 200000 in Codex's picker.** That is the fix, not a regression.

## Action required

None. `mcc-claude`, `mcc-codex` and `mcc-pi` take the same arguments and build byte-identical environments (proof below). `~/.fcc/rtk.json` keeps its existing flat `{"claude": …, "codex": …, "pi": …}` shape, so an existing state file loads unchanged.

## Verification

### Launcher byte-identity vs `fork/main`

Every launcher-built env, argv and install hint dumped from both trees by the same script and diffed:

```
$ diff -u base.json pr1.json && echo "LAUNCHER PARITY: byte-identical"
LAUNCHER PARITY: byte-identical

$ sha256sum base.json pr1.json
037448c3f996ee541457780a4cab022204b465430e8386756317caf02db86475 *base.json
037448c3f996ee541457780a4cab022204b465430e8386756317caf02db86475 *pr1.json
```

Covers `build_claude_launcher_command`, `build_minimal_claude_proxy_env`, `build_claude_proxy_env`, `codex_config_args` (with and without a model), `build_model_catalog_config_args`, `build_codex_launcher_command`, `build_codex_launcher_env`, `build_pi_launcher_command`, `build_pi_launcher_env`, `pi_install_hint` on both platforms, and the full Pi passthrough table.

### Real binaries, scratch server on 8199, redirected `HOME`

```
$ HOME=<scratch> uv run mcc-codex --version
codex-cli 0.151.0                       # exit 0; codex accepted the generated catalogue
$ HOME=<scratch> uv run mcc-codex exec --help
Run Codex non-interactively             # exit 0; full config load with -c model_catalog_json=<generated>
```

`codex` 0.151.0 loads the catalogue including the extra top-level `_mcc_defaulted` key without complaint.

```
$ HOME=<scratch> uv run mcc-pi --version
The 'pi' command at C:\Users\...\npm\pi.CMD is not a compatible Pi Coding Agent.
Install Pi with: powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex"
```

Byte-identical to `fork/main`'s output on the same machine — the identity probe and the Windows install hint both still work, now sourced from the registry.

`mcc-claude --help` launches the real Claude Code through the registry path and prints its usage.

### Fan-out and zero-clobber

A provider refresh with unchanged capabilities left the catalogue's mtime untouched (content-compare skip), and no Pi file was created — Pi's model list is process-local by design:

```
$ stat -c '%y' ~/.fcc/codex-model-catalog.json   # before refresh
2026-09-01 17:09:34.051661300 +0300
$ curl -sX POST .../admin/api/providers/custom_acme/test
{"provider_id":"custom_acme","ok":true,"models":[...]}
$ stat -c '%y' ~/.fcc/codex-model-catalog.json   # after refresh
2026-09-01 17:09:34.051661300 +0300
$ ls ~/.fcc/
cache  codex-model-catalog.json  custom_providers.json  logs
```

Nothing under the real `~/.fcc`, `~/.codex`, `~/.pi` or `~/.claude` was written, and the live 8082 install was never touched.

### Browser drive (Chrome DevTools, 1440×1000 and 700×1000, Midnight and Paper)

- Nav renders `Coding agents` between `Configure Claude Code` and `Model Config`; three cards, correct badges, long catalogue path wraps inside the card.
- The RTK checkboxes on the Providers page render from the harness list as `Claude Code` / `Codex CLI` / `Pi` with ids `rtkAgent-<id>`.
- Not-installed state re-rendered live in the browser: badge flips, the vendor's own install line appears, no button that would run it, and `Last written: Never - written on the first mcc-codex`.
- 700px: single-column stack, `document.body.scrollWidth === clientWidth` (no horizontal overflow).
- **Zero console errors and zero warnings** on the page.

### Tests

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `uv run ruff format --check .` | 1019 files already formatted |
| `uv run ruff check .` | All checks passed |
| `uv run ty check` (repo-wide) | All checks passed |
| `uv run pytest -q` | 8158 passed, 38 skipped, **16 failed** |

15 of those 16 are this machine's known pre-existing failures: 8 websearch tests that read the real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests, and `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. The 16th (`tests/cli/test_desktop_rtk.py::test_toggle_survives_concurrent_external_write`) passes in isolation and across three consecutive `tests/cli/` runs; it fails only under full-suite `xdist` load alongside a pre-existing pystray teardown warning (`'Icon' object has no attribute '_icon_handle'`).

jsdom: `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` **166 passed** run serially (159 before this PR, 7 added). The harness must be run alone — it takes ~70 s and sits near its 180 s timeout under parallel load.

New tests:

- `tests/cli/test_harness_registry.py` — 12: console-script agreement both ways, unique binaries, catalogue-filename constant, RTK capability, T1/T2/T3 launcher parity, and `test_missing_binary_exits_127_with_install_hint` parametrised over every harness.
- `tests/application/test_catalogue_model.py` — 7, including `test_catalogue_models_and_v1_models_agree_on_visible_refs`.
- `tests/application/test_codex_serialiser.py` — 10, including `test_context_window_comes_from_ladder_not_two_hundred_k`, `test_xhigh_absent_when_model_does_not_support_it`, `test_mandatory_reasoning_model_has_no_off_option`, `test_defaulted_fields_are_recorded_in_the_file`.
- `tests/application/test_pi_serialiser.py` — 6.
- `tests/application/test_serialiser_contract.py` — 6, including the static AST guard `test_no_serialiser_hard_codes_a_limit` that fails on any large integer literal bound to a limit-shaped key outside `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS`.
- `tests/runtime/test_catalogue_fanout.py` — 9, including `test_capability_change_alone_re_emits_every_catalogue` and `test_one_serialiser_raising_does_not_abort_the_others_or_the_refresh`.
- `tests/api/test_admin_harnesses.py` — 7 for the two routes.
- `tests/scripts/test_installer_harnesses.py` — 10, including `test_installers_never_install_a_third_party_cli`.
- `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` — 7 jsdom cases; `tests/contracts/test_admin_static_xss.py` — 1 escaping case for the card.
- RTK migration cases added to `tests/config/test_rtk.py`.

Deleted with their subjects: `tests/cli/test_codex_model_catalog.py`, `tests/runtime/test_codex_catalog.py`.

## Deviations from the spec

- **Serialisers live in `application/catalogues/`, not `cli/harnesses/catalogues/`.** `cli` may only import `config` and `core`, so a serialiser there could not have imported `CatalogueModel`. The AST guard scans the package where they actually are.
- **`config/harnesses.py`, not `cli/harnesses/registry.py`, holds the specs.** `api` may not import `cli`, and the dashboard has to list harnesses. `cli/harnesses/registry.py` exists and holds the launcher-side binding.
- **The route returns each CLI's serialised document as well as the neutral records.** Same reason: a launcher cannot import the serialisers, so the server runs them and the launcher writes bytes. This also removes any chance of the two paths drifting.
- **`ensure_exists` still creates `~/.fcc/codex-model-catalog.json` at startup**, behind an explicit `created_at_startup` flag on the spec. Q8's rule is otherwise implemented as written; the exception exists because the Codex *App* reads that file from a persistent `config.toml` and has no launcher, so the documented behaviour would have regressed.
- **`write_json_document_atomically` now writes bytes instead of text.** `Path.write_text` translates `\n` to CRLF on Windows, which would have made the same document differ from itself across platforms and defeated the content-compare skip. This also preserves the old Codex writer's LF output.

## Residual risks

- **The Pi extension's runtime path is unverified.** `projectMccCatalogueModels` is exercised only by the route's own contents and the Python-side unit tests; no Pi session was launched, because the only `pi` on this machine's `PATH` is an unrelated npm package that the identity probe correctly rejects. The extension keeps a `/v1/models` fallback with a `console.warn`, so an older proxy or a route failure degrades to the previous behaviour rather than failing to load.
- **`supports_parallel_tool_calls` is recorded as defaulted for most models**, because only OpenRouter-dialect gateways publish `supported_parameters`. It is honest but noisy in the `_mcc_defaulted` block.
- **Codex's tolerance of the extra `_mcc_defaulted` top-level key is verified against 0.151.0 only.** If a future Codex rejects unknown keys, the block has to move out of the file (the dashboard and stderr copies are independent of it).
- **The tray menu's Codex entry is now labelled "Codex CLI"** rather than "Codex", because labels come from the registry's display names. Cosmetic and deliberate.
- **`test_toggle_survives_concurrent_external_write` flaked once under full-suite load.** It passes in isolation and on three consecutive directory runs; the pystray teardown warning it sits beside is pre-existing.

commit.message:
feat(harnesses): one registry per coding agent, and real model metadata in every catalogue it generates

Broken: every catalogue MCC generated for a coding agent contained the same
invented numbers for every model. `_codex_catalog_entry` built the same dict
for each entry, varying only slug, display name and priority -- every model
claimed `"context_window": 200000`, the same fixed four reasoning rungs, and
`"input_modalities": ["text"]`. Pi's bundled extension did the same one level
down with `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 128000`, `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 16384` and
zero costs. On a scratch server holding an 8k model, a 128k model, a 400k model
and a 1M model, Codex's picker was told all four were 200000. Separately, the
three harness ids were written out by hand in pyproject.toml, both installers
(three lists each), mcc-help, RtkState, the RTK CLI, the tray menu and the
dashboard: eight places to forget one.

Mechanism: both writers consumed `GET /v1/models`, whose `ModelResponse`
carries an id, a display name and no capability fields whatsoever, and both run
in launcher processes that have no `RequestRuntimePort`. The resolution ladder
already resolved per-model context length, output ceiling, vision, tool support
and effort vocabulary -- and rendered all of it on the Models page -- but the
code that had to publish it could not reach it, so it could not have told the
truth even in principle.

Fix: `config/harnesses.py` declares each CLI once and every surface is
generated from or checked against it. `application/catalogue_model.py` builds
one neutral `CatalogueModel` per routable model from the ladder, reusing
`build_models_list_response`'s visibility filter, ref enumeration and
two-variant projection so the two cannot drift. `application/catalogues/`
holds one thin serialiser per CLI: effort vocabularies are intersected with the
CLI's own rungs and never extended, an unknown omits an optional key rather
than writing a zero, and a required field takes that CLI's own documented
default from a module-level `CLI_DOCUMENTED_DEFAULTS` and is recorded in the
file's `_mcc_defaulted` block, on the launcher's stderr and on the dashboard
card. A new loopback-only `GET /admin/api/catalogue-models` serves the neutral
records plus each CLI's serialised document, so launchers write bytes the
server produced instead of reimplementing a mapping.
`runtime/harness_catalogues.py` replaces the single Codex publisher on the same
`cache_model_infos` hook, so a capability change with no change to the model
list now re-emits every materialised catalogue. `RtkState` becomes a mapping
keyed by harness id -- the on-disk format is unchanged -- and the two
atomic-write implementations are consolidated onto `config/atomic_json.py`,
which now writes bytes so a document does not differ from itself across
platforms.

Verification: every launcher-built env, argv and install hint dumped from this
tree and from fork/main and diffed -- byte-identical, sha256
037448c3f996ee541457780a4cab022204b465430e8386756317caf02db86475 on both.
Against a scratch server on 8199 with a redirected HOME and a stub upstream,
`mcc-codex --version` and `mcc-codex exec --help` both exit 0 with the
generated catalogue loaded by the real codex-cli 0.151.0, and the same four
models come out at 8192 / 128000 / 400000 / 1000000 instead of 200000 each,
with `gpt-5-nano` losing the `xhigh` rung it never claimed and `gpt-4o` getting
no effort list at all. A provider refresh with unchanged capabilities left the
file's mtime untouched and created no file for Pi. The Coding agents page and
the generated RTK toggles were driven in Chrome at 1440px and 700px in two
themes with zero console errors. 55 new tests; ruff, ty and 8158 pytest cases
pass, with this machine's 15 known pre-existing failures unchanged.

Not done: the Pi extension's runtime path is covered by unit tests and by the
route's contents, not by a launched Pi session -- the only `pi` on this
machine's PATH is an unrelated npm package the identity probe correctly
rejects. No new CLI is added here; that is PR 2 onwards.

docs(architecture): correct the startup catalogue paragraph for the fan-out publisher

The paragraph still described a warm-start path that creates a minimal catalog
for any caller that warms routed providers first. The fan-out publisher creates
only a catalogue whose spec sets `created_at_startup`, which today is Codex's
alone, because the Codex App reads that file from a persistent config.toml and
has no launcher; every other missing file is left for its own harness's first
launch so MCC leaves nothing behind for a CLI the user does not run.
